narrative:
On September 28, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 3,039 cases across 51 judges, hearing 1,382 of them to post an overall hearing rate of 45.5%. This represents a notable expansion in daily docket volume and a slight efficiency increase compared to preceding court days. The hearing rate previously hovered at 43.4% (1,152 of 2,652 scheduled) on September 25, 43.9% on September 24, and 44.0% on September 23.

Individual judicial performance highlights show significant variance across halls. In Hall 36, Judge T.P. Vivekananda achieved an 82.4% hearing rate, resolving 42 of 51 scheduled cases. In Hall 26, Judge Anant Ramanath Hegde heard 39 out of 50 cases (78.0%), while Judge V. Srishananda in Hall 23 resolved 74 of 105 scheduled matters (70.5%). Handling one of the day's heaviest individual workloads, Judge Sachin Shankar Magadum in Hall 15 successfully heard 89 out of 178 scheduled cases (50.0%). 

Stage-wise conversion insights reveal that cases listed for Orders achieved the highest progress, with 509 out of 965 cases heard (52.7%). Preliminary Hearings followed closely at a 47.8% conversion rate (222 of 464), whereas Final Hearings lagged at 28.0% (177 of 632). 

In terms of case types, Writ Petitions (WP) dominated court dockets, with 1,411 scheduled and 641 heard (45.4%). Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) recorded a 51.6% hearing rate (240 of 465), Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) saw a 44.1% clearance rate (130 of 295), and Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) demonstrated the highest relative clearance among major categories, converting 56.8% (108 of 190) of scheduled matters.
